name: A list pass skips the rows it has already listed, not only the ones fully collected
request: A list pass skips the rows it has already listed, not only the ones fully collected
checks: npm run check passed (typecheck, build, 427 tests, validate)
result: Prerequisite for making the list pass open each applicant, and a loop risk in its own right. createCollectedIndex answers 'is this person COLLECTED', which deliberately means 'carries something substantive' - so a name-only record reads as NOT collected, which is right for a full run (it must still open them) and wrong for the list pass itself, since every record that pass writes is name-only. The collected test therefore always answered no and a resumed list pass re-walked the whole job from the first row. Harmless while a row cost a millisecond; not harmless once a row costs tens of seconds, and actively a loop once an interrupted run continues itself - a pass that keeps being interrupted would walk page one over and over, and because the re-saves read as progress they clear the very fruitless-return budget that would otherwise stop it. Added createListedIndex(), which asks 'do I already HAVE them' by delegating to createCollectedIndex with anyRecord, so there is one keying rule and one job-scoping rule rather than two copies. loadCollectedIndex takes { listed } and picks the builder, so the payload is fetched once either way and the empty fallback keeps the same shape. The worker's PV_APPLICANT_COLLECTED reply no longer filters on the verdict - it sends every stored entry with collected beside it - because a page filtering on that flag can never tell 'already listed' from 'never seen'; the extra entries are three small fields each. createCollectedIndex is unchanged for the full run, and a test asserts the two indexes stay distinguishable, since conflating them would make a full run walk past people it never collected.
